subject: Culture
title: The Camino de Santiago
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Camino de Santiago.

hook.text: In 2019, 350,000 people walked the Camino de Santiago. Most weren't Catholic. Many weren't even religious.

buildup.text: The Camino has been walked since the 9th century, when the bones of St. James were reportedly found in Spain.

discovery.text: The route stretches 800 km across northern Spain. Medieval pilgrims took months; today hikers take about five weeks.

twist.text: Studies show Camino walkers report lasting personality changes—more openness and less materialism six months later.

climax.text: The Camino survived wars, plagues, and secularization. Walking itself became the sacred act.

punchline.text: The path matters more than the destination.

quiz.question: Whose bones are believed to be at Santiago de Compostela?

details.summary: The Camino de Santiago is a network of pilgrimage routes culminating at the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela in Spain, where the apostle Saint James is believed to be buried.
details.whyItMatters: The Camino's recent popularity explosion — from 2,000 pilgrims in 1985 to over 400,000 annually — shows that the human need for transformative pilgrimage persists even in a secular age.
takeaways: The Camino has been walked for over 1,000 years
The most popular route (Camino Francés) covers 780 km across northern Spain
Pilgrim numbers have surged from 2,000 in 1985 to 400,000+ today

faq.question: How long does the Camino take?
faq.answer: The most popular route, the Camino Francés from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port in France to Santiago, covers 780 km and takes 30-35 days walking 20-25 km per day. Shorter routes include the Camino Portugués (240 km from Porto, ~10 days).

faq.question: Do you have to be religious to walk the Camino?
faq.answer: No. While originally a Catholic pilgrimage, today's Camino attracts people of all faiths and none. Many walk for personal challenge, grief processing, life transitions, or simple adventure. The Cathedral requires only walking the last 100 km (or cycling 200 km) to earn the Compostela certificate.
